content.value_statement: Lark attendance data can be hard to check from a chat workflow. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code query personal punch records through lark-cli.
actual_capabilities: Queries personal attendance punch records with the attendance user_tasks query API.
Uses lark-cli as the required command-line interface.
Keeps employee_type fixed as employee_no for attendance requests.
Keeps user_ids empty so the query targets the current authorized user.
Requires schema inspection before native attendance API calls.
Identifies the readonly attendance permission scope needed for the query.
limitations: Requires lark-cli, authentication, and attendance API access to be configured first.
Covers attendance record queries only, not record creation or correction.
Only documents the user_tasks query resource in this skill.
Returned fields depend on the current lark-cli schema and tenant permissions.

use_cases.title: Check Daily Punches
use_cases.description: Review today's check-in and check-out records from Lark without opening the attendance console.

use_cases.title: Prepare Timesheet Review
use_cases.description: Collect recent personal attendance entries before completing a weekly or monthly timesheet review.

use_cases.title: Support Attendance Questions
use_cases.description: Help an operations user verify which readonly scope and query path are needed for attendance lookup.

prompt_templates.title: Check Today
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single day.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show my Lark attendance punch records for today. Use the attendance skill and summarize the check-in and check-out times.

prompt_templates.title: Review Date Range
prompt_templates.prompt: Query my Lark attendance records from Monday through Friday this week. Group the results by date and highlight missing punches.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Query Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Before querying attendance, check the current lark-cli schema and confirm the readonly scope needed for user task records.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Monthly Attendance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Lark attendance records for last month. Summarize late arrivals, early departures, missing punches, and dates that need follow-up.

output_examples.input: Show my attendance records for today.
output_examples.output: Today's attendance shows one morning check-in and one evening check-out. No missing punch was found in the returned records.

output_examples.input: Review my attendance for this week.
output: Monday through Thursday include complete check-in and check-out records.
Friday has no check-out record in the returned data.
The query used the current user context with readonly attendance access.

output_examples.input: What permission do I need for this query?
output_examples.output: The attendance user task query requires readonly access for attendance task records. Tenant policy may require an administrator to grant it.

best_practices: Confirm lark-cli authentication before requesting attendance data.
Run schema inspection when the attendance API shape may have changed.
Ask for a clear date range to avoid broad or slow attendance queries.
anti_patterns: Do not request attendance records for other users with this skill.
Do not guess API fields without checking the current schema.
Do not use the skill to modify, create, or delete attendance records.

faq.question: What does this skill query?
faq.answer: It queries personal Lark attendance punch records through the user task attendance API.

faq.question: Does it require lark-cli?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata requires the lark-cli binary and configured Lark authentication.

faq.question: Can it update attendance records?
faq.answer: No. The documented capability is readonly querying of attendance punch records.

faq.question: Can it query other employees?
faq.answer: No. The skill keeps user_ids empty and uses the authorized user context.

faq.question: Which permission is listed?
faq.answer: The skill lists attendance task readonly access for the user_tasks query method.

faq.question: Why inspect the schema first?
faq.answer: Schema inspection helps confirm current parameters before sending an attendance API request.
